sections.h2: What is Chesterfield like, and what do houses cost here?
sections.html:
Chesterfield is a western suburb of St. Louis in St. Louis County, about 25 miles from downtown, and the Census Bureau counted an estimated 49,309 people on July 1, 2025. It incorporated in 1988 and was the state's 14th largest city at the 2020 census.

It is the priciest of the four Missouri cities in this series, and its population slipped 1.4 percent from the April 2020 estimates base. Owners here are older and have higher incomes than in the other three cities, which shapes who looks at a house for sale.

A quarter of residents are 65 or older, so many Chesterfield sellers are downsizing or settling an estate rather than relocating for work.

The city covers 31.88 square miles of land, with 2.35 people per household, and retail sales of about $30,747 per resident in 2022. Median monthly owner costs run $2,464 with a mortgage and $946 without one, which tells you what a buyer will weigh against your asking price.

sections.h2: How did Chesterfield come together as a city?
sections.html:
Chesterfield was built from several small communities. Bellefontaine, nicknamed Hilltown, dates to about 1837. Lake began as Hog Hollow around 1850, Gumbo grew in the river valley at what is now Chesterfield Airport Road and Long Road, and Monarch sprang up along the Rock Island rail line in the late 1870s.

The valley was once called Gumbo Flats because the silty soil turns to mud when wet. A violent F4 tornado crossed St. Louis County on January 24, 1967, and the area was submerged in the Great Flood of 1993. Higher levees followed, and the valley is now commercial, with Spirit of St. Louis Airport and a long outdoor strip of stores.

The practical point for sellers is that parts of the city sit in the Missouri River floodplain. Ask your lender or title company whether your parcel needs flood insurance.

sections.h2: Who lives in Chesterfield, and what do they ask of a house?
sections.html:
Census figures show a settled, well-connected community. About 86.8 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, 96.5 percent of households have broadband, and poverty sits at 3.9 percent.

  • Foreign-born residents make up 16.0 percent of the population, and 16.1 percent speak a language other than English at home.
  • Asian residents are 13.2 percent of the city, the highest share among the four Missouri cities in this series.
  • Veterans number 2,141.

Education is a draw. Logan University offers chiropractic and rehabilitation programs in the city, and Chesterfield Montessori School, Ascension School and Incarnate Word School serve younger children alongside the public districts. Barat Academy, a private high school, closed in 2025.

sections.h2: Which schools, employers and roads matter to a Chesterfield buyer?
sections.html:
Two districts serve the city. Rockwood School District covers the western part and Parkway School District covers the east, and schools inside the city include Parkway Central, Parkway West and Marquette high schools. Buyers often ask the district first, so put it in your notes.

The city's 2013 financial report named St. Luke's Hospital (3,447 employees), Parkway School District, Bayer, Delmar Gardens and Reinsurance Group of America among its largest employers. Dierbergs, Amdocs and MOHELA appear on the same list.

  • Interstate 64, called Highway 40 locally, has seven exits in the city.
  • Missouri Route 340, or Olive Boulevard, runs east and west through town, and Route 141 forms the eastern edge with Town and Country.
  • Faust Park, with the Butterfly House and a carousel, and the Chesterfield Amphitheater are the best known recreation sites.

sections.h2: Do you need a city permit to repair or sell a Chesterfield house?
sections.html:
Repairs and additions go through the city's Planning Department. Its page describes a building permit as the way to confirm a project is structurally sound and meets building and zoning codes. Call the department before work on structure, additions or exterior changes.

The city's occupancy permit requirement is written for businesses: a permit or re-occupancy permit applies to every new business and every change of business use, tenancy or ownership. If you own a commercial space or a mixed property, that rule matters to your buyer. For an ordinary house sale, ask Chesterfield's Planning Department whether any permit applies to your address.

The city says its occupancy approvals check compliance with city, county and fire district codes, so expect more than one office to be involved. Close any open permit before you list.

sections.h2: How do St. Louis County property taxes work for a Chesterfield seller?
sections.html:
The St. Louis County Assessor values every parcel, and state law section 137.115 requires reassessment as of January 1 of each odd-numbered year. The county Board of Equalization is independent of the assessor. Appeals must be filed or postmarked by the second Monday in July, and the 2026 date was July 13, 2026, which has passed.

The Collector of Revenue bills property tax, and it must be paid or postmarked by December 31 of the billed year. Payments made after that date are subject to up to 18 percent annual interest plus a 2 percent penalty under Missouri law, according to the collector's delinquent tax page.

Property tax is a lien on the house, so a title company will confirm the current year before closing. Ask the collector's office for the exact balance on your parcel.

sections.h2: Where is a Chesterfield deed recorded, and what does it cost?
sections.html:
Deeds for Chesterfield are recorded with the St. Louis County Recorder of Deeds, 41 S. Central Avenue, Clayton, MO 63105. You can mail or drop off the original notarized document with a check or money order made out to ROD, or use an approved eRecording vendor.

The county charges $26 on page one and $3 on every page after it, and adds $25 when a document ignores the state's formatting standards. The original comes back within about a week of recording. Most owners leave this step to the title company.

sections.h2: What are your choices for selling a Chesterfield house quickly?
sections.html:
Because values are high and buyers are choosy, a Chesterfield house in good condition can attract the open market and sell on an agent's listing. A house that needs a kitchen, roof or systems work, or one tied up in an estate, may do better with a direct as-is purchase where the buyer handles repairs.

Get your payoff letter, county tax statement, school district and any permit history together first. With those in hand, you can compare an agent's net proceeds with a cash offer on equal terms.

faqs.q: Which county records a Chesterfield deed?
faqs.a: St. Louis County, through the Recorder of Deeds at 41 S. Central Avenue in Clayton. A deed costs $26 for the first page and $3 for each extra page.

faqs.q: When are St. Louis County property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 31 of the billed year, with the postmark counting for mailed payments. Later payments accrue up to 18 percent yearly interest plus a 2 percent penalty.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my St. Louis County value this year?
faqs.a: No. The 2026 deadline was July 13, 2026, the second Monday in July. Ask the Equalization board when the next filing window opens.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Chesterfield house in?
faqs.a: Rockwood School District serves the west side of the city and Parkway School District serves the east. Confirm the district for your address with the school district's boundary tools before listing.

faqs.q: Does Chesterfield's occupancy permit apply when I sell my home?
faqs.a: The city's occupancy permit page is aimed at businesses, covering new businesses and changes of use, tenancy or ownership. Call the Planning Department to confirm for your address.
